speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a pediatric patient presenting with a limp and localized pain but no fever or acute distress. To begin our evaluation, can you tell me exactly where on your body it hurts, and does it hurt more when you try to walk or when you are resting?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details, young man. Since the pain is localized to the left knee but the limp suggests a hip issue, does the pain travel up into your hip or groin, or does it stay strictly in the knee? Additionally, have you noticed any swelling or redness in that area?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Transient Synovitis of the Hip (presenting as referred knee pain).

The history of a limp with left knee pain, no fever, and no trauma in a 7-year-old male is classic for a hip pathology referring pain to the knee. I would like to confirm the exam findings before finalizing the care plan; please ensure I perform a full range of motion assessment on the left hip (flexion, abduction, internal rotation) and compare it to the right side.
